items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: And I used to have to share that seat with Shorty Sherock -- which he turned out to be a great buddy of mine after he got out of the band.

ctx.x: What happened was that I went and played one of those (?) gigs in Providence. That's what happened. And when I came back, they wanted to make the deal. I was a little ahead of myself, you know. So in respect, that goes back here. I played those three dates in Providence, and then when they decided on me joining the band as a permanent thing, like an act in it. Like Teddy and Lionel were. They were an act, you know, when they first got in the band.

So that transpired. So they went in the Pennsylvania Hotel, and I opened up there with him. And everything was going along fine. But at the end they used to play this finale; they used to play "One O'Clock Jump." And I used to have to share that seat with Shorty Sherock -- which he turned out to be a great buddy of mine after he got out of the band. But he reneged, man. He said, "Man, I'm not gonna... The cat's taking my solo and I got to share my chair with him, too!" So they got into a beef about it, so they…

It was a funny band. Because I can read anything. And I got in the band, people used to come to me: "What are you doing what that book in front of you? You know you can't read no music." They'd be surprised, heh-heh. Intelligent
